newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco unit in S. African joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco unit in S. African joint venture.

text.p: Tenneco Inc's automotive unit said early Thursday that it has agreed to enter a joint venture with a subsidiary of Metair Investments Ltd to manufacture and market ride control products for automobiles and light commercial vehicles in South Africa.
Terms of the deal, with Metair's Armstrong Holdings Ltd, were not disclosed.
However, as part of the agreement, Tenneco Automotive is to acquire majority ownership in Armstrong. The transaction is expected to close within 30 days.
Armstrong has more than 500 employees, 1996 sales of $30 million, about 60 percent of South Africa's original equipment market and more than 40 percent of the replacement market.

"This joint venture is another strong fit in our strategic plan to serve customers globally," Tenneco Automotive President Thomas Evans said in a statement. "As original equipment manufacturers establish assembly plants around the world, we intend to be there to support their needs locally. This is an excellent opportunity to improve our service to customers and participate in an emerging growth market."

Tenneco said that passenger car and light commercial vehicle production in South Africa is growing significantly to meet domestic demand, as well as that from nearby countries in southern and central Africa and Europe.
